title: The Inaugural Ball
notebook: Kolvar's people watch from the east balcony. Brenner is by the west bar in full dress uniform.
Vael has been circling the foreign table. Perhaps two hours before protocol demands my exit.
Renek has blessed the canapés, unasked.
location: Grand Hall of the Republic, Ashenmere

narrative.text: The Grand Hall of the Republic has not seen a night like this in twenty-nine years. Crystal chandeliers cast warm light across a sea of formal dress and military medals. Every faction, every ambition, every grudge left over from the Halvek years is here — dressed in silk and swallowing champagne.
You stand at the top of the marble staircase, Jonas at your side. For a moment, the room turns. Faces lift. This is your first public appearance as Chancellor.
Six conversations you could have tonight. Six people who want something from you. The question is who you choose to speak with — and what that choice signals to everyone watching.

Chancellor. Room is arranged as expected. Kolvar's people near the east balcony — watching you since you arrived. Archbishop has already blessed the canapés. Unasked. General Brenner is in full dress uniform by the west bar. Vael has been circling the foreign table. You have perhaps two hours before protocol demands your exit. Choose conversations carefully — you cannot speak to everyone.

choices.text: Stay with Jonas. Tonight you are a person, not just a Chancellor.
Find Lucan Vael. He came to this ball for a reason.
Speak with Archbishop Renek. The Church's support will matter.
Find General Brenner. You want to know where the military stands.

narrative.text: You find Jonas near the east windows, holding two glasses — champagne for appearances, water for you. He knows. He always knows.
They are all watching you, you know. Even when they pretend not to.
Let them watch. Tonight I want five minutes of not being Chancellor.
You have about three. Vyktor is already moving toward someone who looks important and uncomfortable.
Then we waste none of it. How are you?
Proud. Worried. Both at once. The usual.
You both laugh. It is the first real laugh of the day. In a room full of calculation, it is the only thing that feels true.
Lucan Vael is exactly where Vyktor said — circling the foreign table, performing ease. He excuses himself the moment he sees you move toward him. That itself is information. He has been waiting.
Chancellor. The Republic looks well on you. I hope the office will be — manageable.
I find most things manageable, Mr. Vael. What brings you to a government ball?
The same thing that brings everyone. To see what kind of government this will be. Whether certain — arrangements — from the previous administration will be honored.
There it is. Not a greeting. An audit.
Every arrangement will be reviewed, Mr. Vael. The ones that served the Republic will continue. The others will not.
Of course. I would expect nothing less from you, Chancellor. I look forward to those reviews.
He smiles and returns to his circle. The conversation lasted four minutes. You are fairly certain it will define your relationship with him for the next four years.

choices.text: Give him nothing. Let him wonder.

narrative.text: Archbishop Renek stands near the chapel alcove as if the building has provided him sanctuary. He does not come to you. You go to him. This is already a negotiation.
Chancellor. The Church prays for this government as we have prayed for seventeen before it. We are a patient institution.
I hope patience will not be necessary, Archbishop. I intend to move quickly on several fronts.
Speed and righteousness do not always travel together. The education reform proposals circulating in your coalition — the Church has concerns.
Those proposals are early drafts. Nothing has been decided.
Good. Then there is still time for conversation. The Church is watching this government with hope, Chancellor. We would prefer to keep it that way.
A warning delivered in the language of goodwill. He is better at this than you expected.
General Brenner is near the west bar, not drinking, actively uncomfortable in formal dress. He straightens when he sees you approach — not a bow, a soldier's acknowledgment.
Chancellor. I will be direct — I am better at it than at parties. The military has no political position. We serve the Republic. We serve whoever holds this office.
I appreciate that, General. And I intend to be worth serving.
Good. Then I have one item. The Tyvaren repositioning at Gravenmark. When you are ready to discuss it seriously — not at a ball, in a room with maps — I am available. Day or night.
Tomorrow morning. My office. Seven o'clock.
I will be there at six fifty-five.
He returns to his post by the bar. You like him immediately. In your experience, that is either a very good sign or a warning you will only understand later.

choices.text: Schedule the meeting. Tonight is for appearances.
